source_metadata.title: Minimum standards for rental properties

sections.heading: Minimum standards for rental properties
heading_path: Minimum standards for rental properties

blocks.text: Landlords and agents are required to make sure rental properties meet 7 minimum standards for tenants to be able to live there.

Landlords must provide rental properties that are in a reasonable state of cleanliness and fit for the tenant to live in. The minimum standards set clearer expectations for landlords and tenants and apply to all rented residential properties. To be fit to live in, the property must, at a minimum:
be structurally sound
have adequate natural or artificial lighting in each room, except storage rooms or garages
have adequate ventilation
be supplied with electricity or gas, and have enough electricity or gas sockets for lighting, heating and other appliances
have adequate plumbing and drainage
have a water connection that can supply hot and cold water for drinking, washing and cleaning
have bathroom facilities, including toilet and washing facilities that allow users' privacy.
Landlords need to ensure their rented properties meet these minimum standards to be fit to live in.

The property could have other issues that may make it unfit for a tenant to live in, even if it meets the above seven minimum standards. Before the property is rented out, the landlord or agent should take steps (such as making repairs ) to make sure the property is fit to live in.

links.text: making repairs

blocks.text: These standards must be maintained throughout the tenancy.

title: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties

source_metadata.title: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties

sections.heading: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties
heading_path: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties

blocks.text: A full list of what repairs are considered by law to be urgent in a rental property.

sections.heading: What are considered to be 'urgent repairs'?
heading_path: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties
What are considered to be 'urgent repairs'?

blocks.text: Under the NSW residential tenancy laws, an 'urgent repair' means:
a gas leak
a dangerous electrical fault
flooding or serious flood damage
serious storm or fire damage
a failure or breakdown of the gas, electricity or water supply to the property
a failure or breakdown of any essential service for hot water, cooking, heating, cooling or laundering
a fault or damage which makes the property unsafe or insecure
a burst water service
an appliance, fitting or fixture that uses water or is used to supply water that is broken or not functioning properly, so that a substantial amount of water is being wasted
a blocked or broken toilet
a serious roof leak.
This rule does not include work needed to repair premises that are owned by a person other than the landlord or a person having superior title (such as a head landlord) to the landlord.
Smoke alarms are also considered 'urgent' to ensure they are working, but there are different rules about their repair. Get more information about repair and maintenance of smoke alarms .

links.text: Get more information about repair and maintenance of  smoke alarms

sections.heading: Tenants' responsibilities
heading_path: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties
Tenants' responsibilities

blocks.text: The tenant must notify the landlord or agent of urgent repair needs straight away.

If the landlord or agent does not fix the problem then tenants need to refer to their tenancy agreement to get details of approved repairers. Tenants can then follow the steps to getting urgent repairs done .

title: Getting repairs done on a rental property

source_metadata.title: Getting repairs done on a rental property

sections.heading: Getting repairs done on a rental property
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property

blocks.text: Learn the steps to follow if you want to request urgent or non-urgent repairs to a rental property while you are a tenant.

sections.heading: How do I request a repair be made?
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
How do I request a repair be made?

blocks.text: There are two types of repairs: urgent repairs and non-urgent repairs .

links.text: urgent repairs
non-urgent repairs

blocks.text: In both circumstances you should contact your landlord or real estate agent first.

If you require urgent repairs and you can't contact your landlord or agent, then you can contact a repair person yourself - see your residential tenancy agreement for approved or preferred tradespeople to use - and have the costs reimbursed up to $1,000.

links.text: residential tenancy agreement

sections.heading: What is an 'urgent repair'?
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
What is an 'urgent repair'?

blocks.text: Urgent repairs are for any issue that threatens a property's structural integrity, poses a risk to lives, makes a property unsafe or insecure, or prevents access to essential services.
gas leak
dangerous electrical fault
failure or breakdown of gas, electricity or water supply
burst water service or serious leak
blocked or broken toilet
flooding or serious flood damage
serious storm damage
serious fire damage
serious roof damage or leak
stove or oven
heater or air conditioner
failure or breakdown of hot water service
smoke alarms not working

links.text: smoke alarms not working

blocks.text: See a full list of urgent repair types

links.text: See a full list of urgent repair types

sections.heading: Request repairs from the landlord or agent
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
Request repairs from the landlord or agent

blocks.text: Tell them – in writing if possible – about what needs fixing.

sections.heading: Follow up if you do not hear back
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
Follow up if you do not hear back

blocks.text: Follow up any conversations in writing.

sections.heading: Keep a copy of your requests
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
Keep a copy of your requests

blocks.text: Keep a copy of any correspondence or conversations as evidence.

sections.heading: If you don't hear back, check your lease for repair contacts
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
If you don't hear back, check your lease for repair contacts

blocks.text: If your landlord or agent cannot be contacted or is unwilling or taking too long to arrange repairs, check whether your lease includes details of a preferred tradesperson.

sections.heading: Get the repairs done
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
Get the repairs done

blocks.text: Get the repair work done by a licensed tradesperson, preferably one that has been recommended on your lease.
Your landlord or agent may not have to reimburse you for the cost of the repair if:
you caused the damage

links.text: caused the damage

blocks.text: you didn’t try to contact them about the repair
you didn’t give them a reasonable amount of time to organise the repair
the repair was not carried out by a licensed tradesperson.

sections.heading: Send details of repairs and costs to your landlord or agent
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
Send details of repairs and costs to your landlord or agent

blocks.text: Make sure you send written details of repairs, including receipts for the costs, so you can get repaid.

sections.heading: Get paid back up to $1,000 within 14 days
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get urgent repairs done
Get paid back up to $1,000 within 14 days

blocks.text: You can get repaid for the cost of the work up to $1,000. Your landlord or agent must pay you back within 14 days of your notice.

sections.heading: What is a 'non-urgent' repair?
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
What is a 'non-urgent' repair?

blocks.text: Non-urgent repairs are those that do not need fixing right away. For example, a broken cupboard or a cracked glass window. They are not threatening the property's structure or endangering lives, but will need to be done to keep the property in reasonable condition .

links.text: property in reasonable condition

sections.heading: Request repairs from the landlord or agent
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get non-urgent repairs done
Request repairs from the landlord or agent

blocks.text: Tell them in writing what needs fixing and by when – give a clear deadline.
If you deal with a property agent, you can:
ask the property agency
contact the agency licence holder (the principal or manager)
contact your landlord direct.

sections.heading: Follow up if you do not hear back
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get non-urgent repairs done
Follow up if you do not hear back

blocks.text: Follow up if you have not heard back within a reasonable time frame.

sections.heading: Keep a copy of your requests
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get non-urgent repairs done
Keep a copy of your requests

blocks.text: Keep a copy of any correspondence and a record of any conversations as evidence that you told the landlord/agent.

sections.heading: The landlord or agent should arrange for the repairs to be done
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Steps to get non-urgent repairs done
The landlord or agent should arrange for the repairs to be done

blocks.text: You may need to give your landlord or agent access to the property to assess the repair needs. Tradespeople will also need to get access to do the repairs. There are minimum notice periods for access to rental properties.

links.text: give your landlord or agent access
minimum notice periods

sections.heading: Can you organise non-urgent repairs yourself?
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
Can you organise non-urgent repairs yourself?

blocks.text: If you want to organise for repairs yourself, you need to:
have the landlord’s consent.
ask the landlord to pay you for any costs.
get their consent and agreement to pay in writing.
They should pay you back within 14 days.

sections.heading: What if things go wrong?
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
What if things go wrong?

blocks.text: If urgent repairs are not done:
do not stop paying the rent. If you stop paying your rent , you will be in breach of your lease agreement, and you could be asked to move out.

links.text: stop paying your rent

blocks.text: For urgent repairs, you need to show that:
the problem needing repair was not your fault
you made a ‘reasonable’ attempt to contact the landlord/agent
you allowed the landlord or agent a ‘reasonable’ chance to do the repairs
a repair person named in your tenancy agreement (if possible) or a licensed or qualified tradesperson did the repairs
you have copies of all receipts and records of conversations or letters that you have written.
You will need to have your landlord or agent's agreement if any non-urgent repairs are needed and follow the steps outlined above to get them done.

links.text: follow the steps outlined above

blocks.text: If a repair issue is not able to be resolved, you can lodge a complaint to NSW Fair Trading to get help. If the landlord or agent doesn't want to carry out the repairs, NSW Fair Trading may decide to issue a rectification order .

links.text: lodge a complaint to NSW Fair Trading
rectification order

blocks.text: If this still does not solve the issue, you can escalate the dispute to the Tribunal (NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT)).

links.text: dispute to the Tribunal

blocks.text: To get help and support, go to the Tenants’ Union of NSW for legal advice, assistance, and information to tenants, with resources in community languages available. The NSW Aboriginal Tenancy Advice and Advocacy Services also offers assistance and support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander tenants.

links.text: Tenants’ Union of NSW
NSW Aboriginal Tenancy Advice and Advocacy Services

sections.heading: Request advice before a Tribunal hearing
heading_path: Getting repairs done on a rental property
What if things go wrong?
Request advice before a Tribunal hearing

blocks.text: Do you have a date for a hearing in the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT)? Get advice from your local Tenants Advice and Advocacy Service.
Use the Tenants' Union request form .

links.text: Use the Tenants' Union request form

title: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties

source_metadata.title: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties

sections.heading: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties

blocks.text: Landlords have a responsibility to ensure that the property is fit to live in and meets health and safety laws.
Landlords are responsible for:
providing a property that is fit to live in
maintaining the rental property in a reasonable state of repair
providing and maintaining locks or other security devices to ensure the property is reasonably secure.
Landlords who do not comply with these obligations will be in breach of the tenancy agreement.

sections.heading: Repairs and maintenance in a rental property
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Repairs and maintenance in a rental property

blocks.text: Landlords are responsible for repairing and maintaining the property so that it is in a reasonable state of repair, considering:
the age of the property
the amount of rent being paid
the prospective life of the property.
This does not mean that the property must be in perfect condition.
To learn more about landlord obligations for repairs and maintenance, visit Getting repairs done on a rental property .

links.text: Getting repairs done on a rental property

sections.heading: Landlords should deal with urgent repairs
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Situations where landlords are required to make repairs to a rental property
Landlords should deal with urgent repairs

blocks.text: Urgent repairs are considered to be repairs needed for serious issues that make a property unsafe or insecure or prevent access to essential services. That is, an issue that:
threatens a property's structural integrity.
poses a risk to lives.
makes a property unsafe or insecure.
prevents access to essential services.
Visit the Urgent repairs in residential rental properties page to see a list of what is considered an urgent repair.

links.text: Urgent repairs in residential rental properties

sections.heading: Landlords have certain responsibilities after a natural disaster
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Situations where landlords are required to make repairs to a rental property
Landlords have certain responsibilities after a natural disaster

blocks.text: If a property has been affected by a natural disaster, such as a flood, bushfire or storm, landlords have certain responsibilities.
Serious storm, fire or flood damage are all considered to be urgent repairs and should be handled quickly.
Learn more about obligations for landlords after a rental property is affected by a natural disaster .

links.text: Learn more about obligations for landlords after a rental property is affected by a natural disaster

sections.heading: Summary of key obligations for landlords
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms
Summary of key obligations for landlords

blocks.text: Landlords should repair a smoke alarm within certain time frames.
Landlords should conduct checks to ensure the smoke alarm is working.
Landlords should install or replace removable batteries every year.

If the rental property is in a strata scheme, the owners corporation may be responsible for repair and replacement of smoke alarms. Even if that is the case, landlords still have some obligations. See 'Smoke alarms in strata schemes' below.

sections.heading: When are smoke alarms considered not working
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms
Summary of key obligations for landlords
When are smoke alarms considered not working

blocks.text: The smoke alarm is removed and not replaced with a working smoke alarm.
The smoke alarm does not work (for example because the battery needs to be replaced).
The smoke alarm is malfunctioning (for example due to accumulated dust, insects, airborne contaminants or corrosion of electrical circuitry).

sections.heading: Smoke alarms in strata schemes
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms
Summary of key obligations for landlords
Smoke alarms in strata schemes

blocks.text: Landlords with properties in a strata scheme have an obligation to ensure smoke alarms installed in the property are working. If the owners corporation is responsible for the repair and replacement of smoke alarms, landlords may have some different obligations relating to smoke alarms.
Visit the Smoke alarms in a rental property page to learn more about landlord obligations and smoke alarms, including in strata schemes.

links.text: Smoke alarms in a rental property

sections.heading: Non-urgent repairs
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms
Non-urgent repairs

blocks.text: A landlord or agent is responsible for arranging non-urgent repairs needed to comply with the landlord's obligation to maintain a rental property in a reasonable state of repair.

A tenant must have written permission 'to carry out repairs to a rental property, including agreement on any reimbursement for costs, from the landlord, except for urgent repairs and some smoke alarm repairs, but tenants need to follow the requirements for those repairs.

sections.heading: Meeting health and safety laws for a rental property
heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Meeting health and safety laws for a rental property

blocks.text: Landlords have a responsibility to ensure the property meets health and safety laws.
Meeting health and safety laws is a term of every tenancy agreement, and landlords who do not comply with these obligations will be in breach of the agreement.
Learn more about health and safety in a rental home .

links.text: Learn more about health and safety in a rental home

heading_path: Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties
Resolving a repair, maintenance or damage dispute with a tenant

blocks.text: It is always best for landlords or an agent to try and seek a resolution with a tenant . If an issue cannot be resolved, a landlord can:

links.text: seek a resolution with a tenant

lodge an application directly with the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT).

links.text: NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal

blocks.text: In some situations, Fair Trading may issue a rectification order to landlords to undertake repairs, or to tenants to fix damage.

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Situations where landlords are required to make repairs to a rental property > Landlords should deal with urgent repairs
Urgent repairs are considered to be repairs needed for serious issues that make a property unsafe or insecure or prevent access to essential services. That is, an issue that:
threatens a property's structural integrity.
poses a risk to lives.
makes a property unsafe or insecure.
prevents access to essential services.
Visit the Urgent repairs in residential rental properties page to see a list of what is considered an urgent repair.

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Situations where landlords are required to make repairs to a rental property > Landlords have certain responsibilities after a natural disaster
If a property has been affected by a natural disaster, such as a flood, bushfire or storm, landlords have certain responsibilities.
Serious storm, fire or flood damage are all considered to be urgent repairs and should be handled quickly.
Learn more about obligations for landlords after a rental property is affected by a natural disaster .

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms > Summary of key obligations for landlords
Landlords should repair a smoke alarm within certain time frames.
Landlords should conduct checks to ensure the smoke alarm is working.
Landlords should install or replace removable batteries every year.
If the rental property is in a strata scheme, the owners corporation may be responsible for repair and replacement of smoke alarms. Even if that is the case, landlords still have some obligations. See 'Smoke alarms in strata schemes' below.

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms > Summary of key obligations for landlords > When are smoke alarms considered not working
The smoke alarm is removed and not replaced with a working smoke alarm.
The smoke alarm does not work (for example because the battery needs to be replaced).
The smoke alarm is malfunctioning (for example due to accumulated dust, insects, airborne contaminants or corrosion of electrical circuitry).

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms > Summary of key obligations for landlords > Smoke alarms in strata schemes
Landlords with properties in a strata scheme have an obligation to ensure smoke alarms installed in the property are working. If the owners corporation is responsible for the repair and replacement of smoke alarms, landlords may have some different obligations relating to smoke alarms.
Visit the Smoke alarms in a rental property page to learn more about landlord obligations and smoke alarms, including in strata schemes.

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Repairing and maintaining smoke alarms > Non-urgent repairs
A landlord or agent is responsible for arranging non-urgent repairs needed to comply with the landlord's obligation to maintain a rental property in a reasonable state of repair.
A tenant must have written permission 'to carry out repairs to a rental property, including agreement on any reimbursement for costs, from the landlord, except for urgent repairs and some smoke alarm repairs, but tenants need to follow the requirements for those repairs.

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Meeting health and safety laws for a rental property
Landlords have a responsibility to ensure the property meets health and safety laws.
Meeting health and safety laws is a term of every tenancy agreement, and landlords who do not comply with these obligations will be in breach of the agreement.
Learn more about health and safety in a rental home .

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Resolving a repair, maintenance or damage dispute with a tenant
It is always best for landlords or an agent to try and seek a resolution with a tenant . If an issue cannot be resolved, a landlord can:
contact Fair Trading’s tenancy complaints and disputes service
lodge an application directly with the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT).
In some situations, Fair Trading may issue a rectification order to landlords to undertake repairs, or to tenants to fix damage.

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Resolving a repair, maintenance or damage dispute with a tenant > Get help from NSW Fair Trading
Ask a question, get support, make a complaint, give feedback or get help with a dispute on matters relating to residential tenancies.
NSW Fair Trading call centre: 13 32 20
Monday to Friday, 8:30am-5pm
Make a tenancy or other real estate related enquiry at NSW Fair Trading
Provide feedback or make a complaint to NSW Fair Trading
Get information and advice about dealing with tenancy disputes

Landlord responsibilities for repair and maintenance of rental properties > Legislation supporting this page
Security and safety of residential premises, Part 3 Division 7 Residential Tenancies Act 2010
Landlord’s general obligations for residential premises, Section 52, Residential Tenancies Act 2010

title: How to Fix a Hole In Drywall

source_metadata.title: How to Fix a Hole In Drywall
source_metadata.summary: Have you ever opened a door too hard and it hit...
source_metadata.introduction: Have you ever opened a door too hard and it hit the wall causing a small hole in the wall? This is a problem that so many people have, especially with children in the home. Most modern homes have walls made of a material called drywall. A hole in drywall is very easy to patch. It requires no prior skill or experience. This fix requires inexpensive tools and materials that you may find at a local hardware store or you may even already have some of these items at home. This is a guide  on how to patch a small hole in the wall for beginners. This guide will include a complete step by step guide along with all tools and materials that are needed to complete this task.

lines.text_raw: Use pliers (or [product|IF145-020|tweezers] if the hole is very small) to clean out hole by removing the drywall out of the hole.
lines.text_rendered: Use pliers (or tweezers if the hole is very small) to clean out hole by removing the drywall out of the hole.

lines.text_raw: Use scissors to cut drywall mesh.
lines.text_rendered: Use scissors to cut drywall mesh.

lines.text_raw: To ensure that the entire hole is covered, cut a piece of mesh larger than the size of the hole.
lines.text_rendered: To ensure that the entire hole is covered, cut a piece of mesh larger than the size of the hole.

lines.text_raw: Use a damp sponge to apply moisture to make the mesh stick to the wall, covering the entire hole.
lines.text_rendered: Use a damp sponge to apply moisture to make the mesh stick to the wall, covering the entire hole.

lines.text_raw: Use a drywall knife to apply the drywall compound over the mesh. Make sure to spread a generous amount over the entire mesh.
lines.text_rendered: Use a drywall knife to apply the drywall compound over the mesh. Make sure to spread a generous amount over the entire mesh.

lines.text_raw: Let the compound dry for about 30 minutes.
lines.text_rendered: Let the compound dry for about 30 minutes.

lines.text_raw: You can speed up the drying process by placing a fan directly in front of the drying compound.
lines.text_rendered: You can speed up the drying process by placing a fan directly in front of the drying compound.

lines.text_raw: Once compound is dry, use sandpaper to smooth out the entire surface of the dried compound.
lines.text_rendered: Once compound is dry, use sandpaper to smooth out the entire surface of the dried compound.

lines.text_raw: Paint over the surface with a paint brush.
lines.text_rendered: Paint over the surface with a paint brush.

lines.text_raw: Use paint that matches the rest of the wall for best results.
lines.text_rendered: Use paint that matches the rest of the wall for best results.

title: How To Fix A Leaky Faucet

source_metadata.title: How To Fix A Leaky Faucet
source_metadata.summary: Use this guide to stop a leak in a common...
source_metadata.introduction: Use this guide to stop a leak in a common cartridge faucet.

lines.text_raw: Shut off the hot and cold water valves underneath the sink by twisting them clockwise until they are tight.
lines.text_rendered: Shut off the hot and cold water valves underneath the sink by twisting them clockwise until they are tight.

lines.text_raw: The appearance of these valves will differ from sink to sink, but most operate the same.
lines.text_rendered: The appearance of these valves will differ from sink to sink, but most operate the same.

lines.text_raw: To test that the water has been completely shut off, try turning on the faucet like you would normally. If no water comes out, you're in luck!
lines.text_rendered: To test that the water has been completely shut off, try turning on the faucet like you would normally. If no water comes out, you're in luck!

lines.text_raw: When reopening the valves after the repair, leave the faucet in its on position. This will prevent pressurized air from building up in the faucet cartridge.
lines.text_rendered: When reopening the valves after the repair, leave the faucet in its on position. This will prevent pressurized air from building up in the faucet cartridge.

lines.text_raw: Pull up on the the pop-up drain stopper to seal the sink drain.
lines.text_rendered: Pull up on the the pop-up drain stopper to seal the sink drain.

lines.text_raw: Place a towel in the sink to catch any excess water or faucet hardware.
lines.text_rendered: Place a towel in the sink to catch any excess water or faucet hardware.

lines.text_raw: Use your fingers or a prying tool to remove the plug button from the top of the faucet handle.
lines.text_rendered: Use your fingers or a prying tool to remove the plug button from the top of the faucet handle.

lines.text_raw: Use a screwdriver to remove the single handle screw.
lines.text_rendered: Use a screwdriver to remove the single handle screw.

lines.text_raw: The number and head type/length of the screws may vary from faucet to faucet.
lines.text_rendered: The number and head type/length of the screws may vary from faucet to faucet.

lines.text_raw: Gently pull the faucet handle up from the rest of the faucet.
lines.text_rendered: Gently pull the faucet handle up from the rest of the faucet.

lines.text_raw: Remove the temperature limit stop from the top of the cartridge.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the temperature limit stop from the top of the cartridge.

lines.text_raw: When removing the temperature limit stop and indexer, take note of their position. The limit stop and indexer determine the maximum temperature that water can reach when coming out of the faucet.
lines.text_rendered: When removing the temperature limit stop and indexer, take note of their position. The limit stop and indexer determine the maximum temperature that water can reach when coming out of the faucet.

lines.text_raw: Even if you mark the position of the indexer and stop, you ''may'' still need to [http://www.us.kohler.com/webassets/kpna/catalog/pdf/en/1202228_2.pdf|reset the temperature limit|new_window=true] after addressing the leak. Follow the instructions for your specific faucet if they are available.
lines.text_rendered: Even if you mark the position of the indexer and stop, you may still need to reset the temperature limit after addressing the leak. Follow the instructions for your specific faucet if they are available.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew the bonnet from the faucet.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew the bonnet from the faucet.

lines.text_raw: Remove the temperature limit indexer from the top of the cartridge.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the temperature limit indexer from the top of the cartridge.

lines.text_raw: Use an adjustable wrench to loosen the bonnet nut.
lines.text_rendered: Use an adjustable wrench to loosen the bonnet nut.

lines.text_raw: Remove the bonnet nut.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the bonnet nut.

lines.text_raw: Remove the cartridge.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the cartridge.

lines.text_raw: Remove the cartridge o-rings.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the cartridge o-rings.

lines.text_raw: If the leak has been coming only from the end of the faucet, replace the cartridge.
lines.text_rendered: If the leak has been coming only from the end of the faucet, replace the cartridge.

lines.text_raw: If the faucet has been leaking from the base or from the faucet handle, replace the o-rings.
lines.text_rendered: If the faucet has been leaking from the base or from the faucet handle, replace the o-rings.

lines.text_raw: When installing new o-rings, be sure to properly seat them into the grooves on the underside of the cartridge. A misaligned o-ring can easily cause a new leak.
lines.text_rendered: When installing new o-rings, be sure to properly seat them into the grooves on the underside of the cartridge. A misaligned o-ring can easily cause a new leak.

lines.text_raw: When reinserting the cartridge, be sure that the keys on the cartridge line up with the keys on the base of the faucet.
lines.text_rendered: When reinserting the cartridge, be sure that the keys on the cartridge line up with the keys on the base of the faucet.

title: How to Unclog a Sink Using a Wet Vacuum

source_metadata.title: How to Unclog a Sink Using a Wet Vacuum
source_metadata.summary: If your sink is clogged and you're looking for...
source_metadata.introduction:
If your sink is clogged and you're looking for a quick way to clear it, this guide will walk you through using a wet/dry vacuum to effectively unclog your sink without the need for harsh chemicals or professional assistance.

This method is suitable for most standard sinks. Keep in mind that some stopper plugs are attached to the p-trap and may require extra precautions when removing them. Follow instructions [link|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wj7VZVcoU48&t=7s|here] to learn how to do that. Additionally, some sinks have an overflow hole that should be sealed during this process to maintain proper suction.

Before beginning, make sure your sink is free of standing water and that your vacuum is ready for wet use. If needed, check your vacuum’s settings to ensure it's set up for liquid suction.

tools.text: RIDGID NXT 60L (16 Gal.) 5.0 Peak HP Wet/Dry Shop Vacuum with Filter, Hose and Accessories
tools.wiki_title: RIDGID NXT 60L (16 Gal.) 5.0 Peak HP Wet Dry Shop Vacuum with Filter Hose and Accessories

lines.text_raw: Before starting, make sure your sink is empty.
lines.text_rendered: Before starting, make sure your sink is empty.

lines.text_raw: Clear out the sink using a cup or sponge to remove any standing water for better suction.
lines.text_rendered: Clear out the sink using a cup or sponge to remove any standing water for better suction.

lines.text_raw: If your stopper is attached to the p-trap, removing it may cause water to leak. Be ready to duct tape it or have a towel or small bucket to catch the leak.
lines.text_rendered: If your stopper is attached to the p-trap, removing it may cause water to leak. Be ready to duct tape it or have a towel or small bucket to catch the leak.

lines.text_raw: If your sink has a stopper plug, take it out.
lines.text_rendered: If your sink has a stopper plug, take it out.

lines.text_raw: This will give direct access to the clogged drain and improve suction.
lines.text_rendered: This will give direct access to the clogged drain and improve suction.

lines.text_raw: Most sinks have detached stopper plugs. However, some sink stoppers are connected to the p-trap, so check which type you have and adjust accordingly.
lines.text_rendered: Most sinks have detached stopper plugs. However, some sink stoppers are connected to the p-trap, so check which type you have and adjust accordingly.

lines.text_raw: If your sink has an overflow hole, cover it with duct tape or a towel to seal it.
lines.text_rendered: If your sink has an overflow hole, cover it with duct tape or a towel to seal it.

lines.text_raw: This helps maintain suction and prevents water from leaking through it.
lines.text_rendered: This helps maintain suction and prevents water from leaking through it.

lines.text_raw: Ensure that your vacuum can suck up water, using a regular vacuum could cause damage to the vacuum.
lines.text_rendered: Ensure that your vacuum can suck up water, using a regular vacuum could cause damage to the vacuum.

lines.text_raw: Before setting up, open your wet vacuum so it’s ready for use.
lines.text_rendered: Before setting up, open your wet vacuum so it’s ready for use.

lines.text_raw: Check the settings on your vacuum to see if your filter is good for wet or dry use.
lines.text_rendered: Check the settings on your vacuum to see if your filter is good for wet or dry use.

lines.text_raw: Remove the filter to avoid potential damage.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the filter to avoid potential damage.

lines.text_raw: As a precaution, it's recommended to remove the filter even if it's designed for wet use to prevent potential damage over time.
lines.text_rendered: As a precaution, it's recommended to remove the filter even if it's designed for wet use to prevent potential damage over time.

lines.text_raw: Position the vacuum hose directly over the drain.
lines.text_rendered: Position the vacuum hose directly over the drain.

lines.text_raw: Press the hose firmly against the drain.
lines.text_rendered: Press the hose firmly against the drain.

lines.text_raw: If needed, add an inch of water to the sink before attaching the hose, this can help improve suction.
lines.text_rendered: If needed, add an inch of water to the sink before attaching the hose, this can help improve suction.

lines.text_raw: Switch the vacuum to wet mode and turn it on.
lines.text_rendered: Switch the vacuum to wet mode and turn it on.

lines.text_raw: Hold the hose over the drain for about two minutes to pull up the clog.
lines.text_rendered: Hold the hose over the drain for about two minutes to pull up the clog.

lines.text_raw: The vacuum tank may fill up quickly, so be prepared to empty it once or twice during the process.
lines.text_rendered: The vacuum tank may fill up quickly, so be prepared to empty it once or twice during the process.

lines.text_raw: Check the vacuum hose for debris every few minutes.
lines.text_rendered: Check the vacuum hose for debris every few minutes.

lines.text_raw: If hair or gunk comes up, remove it by hand or with needle-nose pliers before continuing.
lines.text_rendered: If hair or gunk comes up, remove it by hand or with needle-nose pliers before continuing.

lines.text_raw: Remove the hose from the sink.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the hose from the sink.

lines.text_raw: Run water to see if the clog is cleared. If water still drains slowly, repeat the process or consider seeking professional assistance.
lines.text_rendered: Run water to see if the clog is cleared. If water still drains slowly, repeat the process or consider seeking professional assistance.

source_metadata.title: Toilet Flapper Replacement
source_metadata.summary: The toilet flapper opens to allow water to flow...
source_metadata.introduction: The toilet flapper opens to allow water to flow from the toilet tank into the bowl when the toilet is flushed. Afterwards, it closes as the toilet tank fills back up. If water is constantly flowing  from your toilet tank, chances are your flapper is not functioning properly and will require a replacement.

lines.text_raw: Lift the tank lid up and away from the toilet tank.
lines.text_rendered: Lift the tank lid up and away from the toilet tank.

lines.text_raw: Shut off the stop valve underneath the toilet by turning it clockwise until it becomes hand tight.
lines.text_rendered: Shut off the stop valve underneath the toilet by turning it clockwise until it becomes hand tight.

lines.text_raw: The appearance of this valve may differ from toilet to toilet, but most operate the same. Some valves require multiple turns to stop the water while others only require a quarter turn.
lines.text_rendered: The appearance of this valve may differ from toilet to toilet, but most operate the same. Some valves require multiple turns to stop the water while others only require a quarter turn.

lines.text_raw: Push down the flush lever.
lines.text_rendered: Push down the flush lever.

lines.text_raw: Hold the lever down until water stops draining from the tank.
lines.text_rendered: Hold the lever down until water stops draining from the tank.

lines.text_raw: A small amount of water will remain in the bottom of the tank.
lines.text_rendered: A small amount of water will remain in the bottom of the tank.

lines.text_raw: If the flush lever or pull chain have become disconnected, lift up the toilet flapper to drain the tank.
lines.text_rendered: If the flush lever or pull chain have become disconnected, lift up the toilet flapper to drain the tank.

lines.text_raw: Squeeze open the spring clasp that connects the pull chain to the tank lever.
lines.text_rendered: Squeeze open the spring clasp that connects the pull chain to the tank lever.

lines.text_raw: Disconnect the spring clasp from the tank lever.
lines.text_rendered: Disconnect the spring clasp from the tank lever.

lines.text_raw: Disconnect the flapper from the posts on each side of the overflow tube.
lines.text_rendered: Disconnect the flapper from the posts on each side of the overflow tube.

lines.text_raw: Remove the flapper from the toilet tank.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the flapper from the toilet tank.

title: How to Fix Wobbly Toilet Seat Hinges

source_metadata.title: How to Fix Wobbly Toilet Seat Hinges
source_metadata.summary: This guide shows how to fix slow-close toilet...
source_metadata.introduction:
This guide shows how to fix slow-close toilet hinges that have become loosened through extended use. The steps in this guide include removing the toilet seat, taking apart the hinge assembly, tightening the dampers, reassembling the toilet seat, and then putting it back onto the toilet bowl.

The toilet seat used in this guide is a Cachet Round Closed Front Toilet Seat with Q3 Advantage by KOHLER, Model #K-R4639-0, although the instructions apply to many other kinds of toilet seats with slow-close hinges.

A dirty toilet seat can make disassembly both unsanitary and off-putting. To make your repair job as easy as possible, ensure that your toilet seat and hinges are clean before beginning disassembly.

lines.text_raw: Make sure your toilet lid is in the closed position.
lines.text_rendered: Make sure your toilet lid is in the closed position.

lines.text_raw: Locate the plastic hinge covers at the back of the lid.
lines.text_rendered: Locate the plastic hinge covers at the back of the lid.

lines.text_raw: Open both hinges by curling your fingers underneath the plastic overhang at the back of the hinge and pulling straight up. You will now be able to move your toilet seat.
lines.text_rendered: Open both hinges by curling your fingers underneath the plastic overhang at the back of the hinge and pulling straight up. You will now be able to move your toilet seat.

lines.text_raw: With a firm grasp on either side of the toilet seat, pull straight forwards so that the seat slides off the toilet bowl.
lines.text_rendered: With a firm grasp on either side of the toilet seat, pull straight forwards so that the seat slides off the toilet bowl.

lines.text_raw: Place your toilet seat upside-down on a flat surface.
lines.text_rendered: Place your toilet seat upside-down on a flat surface.

lines.text_raw: Locate the hinge assembly towards the back of the toilet seat.
lines.text_rendered: Locate the hinge assembly towards the back of the toilet seat.

lines.text_raw: Your toilet seat might have a plastic covering over the hinge assembly. If so, simply pry it off with your fingers and set it aside for re-installation later.
lines.text_rendered: Your toilet seat might have a plastic covering over the hinge assembly. If so, simply pry it off with your fingers and set it aside for re-installation later.

lines.text_raw: Locate the cylindrical dampers on either side of the hinge assembly.
lines.text_rendered: Locate the cylindrical dampers on either side of the hinge assembly.

lines.text_raw: Using your needle-nose pliers, pinch one of the dampers and pull it halfway out of its compartment, or until the damper no longer connects the hinge assembly to the toilet seat.
lines.text_rendered: Using your needle-nose pliers, pinch one of the dampers and pull it halfway out of its compartment, or until the damper no longer connects the hinge assembly to the toilet seat.

lines.text_raw: Do the same to the other damper.
lines.text_rendered: Do the same to the other damper.

lines.text_raw: With both dampers still in their compartments, remove the hinge assembly from the toilet seat.
lines.text_rendered: With both dampers still in their compartments, remove the hinge assembly from the toilet seat.

lines.text_raw: Place the hinge assembly upside-down on a flat surface.
lines.text_rendered: Place the hinge assembly upside-down on a flat surface.

lines.text_raw: Remove one of the dampers by pushing it out of its compartment with your finger.
lines.text_rendered: Remove one of the dampers by pushing it out of its compartment with your finger.

lines.text_raw: Do the same for the other damper.
lines.text_rendered: Do the same for the other damper.

lines.text_raw: Hold one of the dampers by the smaller end.
lines.text_rendered: Hold one of the dampers by the smaller end.

lines.text_raw: Examine the damper for notches or markings. Some dampers have a set of notches, or arrows, that indicate "Slow/fast". If your dampers have markers like this, use them to determine how far back you want to rotate your dampers.
lines.text_rendered: Examine the damper for notches or markings. Some dampers have a set of notches, or arrows, that indicate "Slow/fast". If your dampers have markers like this, use them to determine how far back you want to rotate your dampers.

lines.text_raw: Some dampers have no notches or markings; if this is the case, you will have to guess at how far back to rotate them. You may need to repeat this step a few times to perfect the tightness of your dampers.
lines.text_rendered: Some dampers have no notches or markings; if this is the case, you will have to guess at how far back to rotate them. You may need to repeat this step a few times to perfect the tightness of your dampers.

lines.text_raw: If there is only one set of notches on the damper, it can not be adjusted.
lines.text_rendered: If there is only one set of notches on the damper, it can not be adjusted.

lines.text_raw: Once you have determined how far back to rotate your damper, insert the large end of the damper back into the hinge assembly, leaving the small end sticking out. This will make it easier to rotate the small end of the damper.
lines.text_rendered: Once you have determined how far back to rotate your damper, insert the large end of the damper back into the hinge assembly, leaving the small end sticking out. This will make it easier to rotate the small end of the damper.

lines.text_raw: Grip your needle-nose pliers in one hand and the hinge assembly in the other.
lines.text_rendered: Grip your needle-nose pliers in one hand and the hinge assembly in the other.

lines.text_raw: Pinch the protruding end of the damper with the needle-nose pliers and twist, rotating it in the direction of the plastic hinge covers. Rotate the dampers until they reach the level of tension you determined in Step 5.
lines.text_rendered: Pinch the protruding end of the damper with the needle-nose pliers and twist, rotating it in the direction of the plastic hinge covers. Rotate the dampers until they reach the level of tension you determined in Step 5.

lines.text_raw: Repeat steps 5-6 with the other damper.
lines.text_rendered: Repeat steps 5-6 with the other damper.

lines.text_raw: Place the hinge assembly back into the toilet seat with the holes aligned.
lines.text_rendered: Place the hinge assembly back into the toilet seat with the holes aligned.

lines.text_raw: Re-insert the damper, small-end first, with your fingers. You should be able to feel the damper sliding into the hinge hole in the toilet seat.
lines.text_rendered: Re-insert the damper, small-end first, with your fingers. You should be able to feel the damper sliding into the hinge hole in the toilet seat.

lines.text_raw: Do the same to the other damper.
lines.text_rendered: Do the same to the other damper.

lines.text_raw: If you removed a plastic cover from the hinge assembly, snap it back into place.
lines.text_rendered: If you removed a plastic cover from the hinge assembly, snap it back into place.

lines.text_raw: With the hinge assembly and toilet seat re-assembled, pick the entire toilet seat back up and align it with the bolts on your toilet bowl.
lines.text_rendered: With the hinge assembly and toilet seat re-assembled, pick the entire toilet seat back up and align it with the bolts on your toilet bowl.

lines.text_raw: Push straight forward, until the hinges audibly click back into place.
lines.text_rendered: Push straight forward, until the hinges audibly click back into place.

lines.text_raw: Finally, close the plastic hinge covers.
lines.text_rendered: Finally, close the plastic hinge covers.

lines.text_raw: Finally, unlock the connector (e.g. with your nails or a flat-blade screwdriver) and pull it out.

lines.text_raw: Put the control panel aside.
lines.text_rendered: Put the control panel aside.

lines.text_raw: The drum is freely suspended. Wedge a towel on the rear side behind the drum to immobilize it. This will prevent damage when tilting the washing machine later on.
lines.text_rendered: The drum is freely suspended. Wedge a towel on the rear side behind the drum to immobilize it. This will prevent damage when tilting the washing machine later on.

lines.text_raw: ***DO NOT FORGET TO REMOVE THIS when reassembling!***
lines.text_rendered: DO NOT FORGET TO REMOVE THIS when reassembling!

steps.title: Detach door seal from front cover

lines.text_raw: The rubber door seal is attached to the front cover by a metal wire and a spring.
lines.text_rendered: The rubber door seal is attached to the front cover by a metal wire and a spring.

lines.text_raw: Pry out the spring and pull away the wire.
lines.text_rendered: Pry out the spring and pull away the wire.

lines.text_raw: Unpeel the seal all the way round, and tuck it inside.
lines.text_rendered: Unpeel the seal all the way round, and tuck it inside.

steps.title: Remove drain/filter door, drain water, and unscrew

lines.text_raw: The round door (front bottom right) for the drain tube and filter can be removed, by opening it completely, and gently pulling out the left side of the hinge.
lines.text_rendered: The round door (front bottom right) for the drain tube and filter can be removed, by opening it completely, and gently pulling out the left side of the hinge.

lines.text_raw: '''DRAIN ANY REMAINING WATER'''.
lines.text_rendered: DRAIN ANY REMAINING WATER.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew two T20 screws.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew two T20 screws.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew two (T20) screws at the top.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew two (T20) screws at the top.

lines.text_raw: Tilt the whole washing machine towards its rear side to expose the front bottom. Lean it against a wall.
lines.text_rendered: Tilt the whole washing machine towards its rear side to expose the front bottom. Lean it against a wall.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew two (6mm hex-head) screws on the bottom.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew two (6mm hex-head) screws on the bottom.

lines.text_raw: The front cover is held in place by plastic hooked pins. Slightly lift the front cover to unhook it.
lines.text_rendered: The front cover is held in place by plastic hooked pins. Slightly lift the front cover to unhook it.

lines.text_raw: On the inside, unclip something, and pull out a connector (for the door lock). The plastic emergency door release comes out easily. The image shows this when clip and connector are already disconnected.
lines.text_rendered: On the inside, unclip something, and pull out a connector (for the door lock). The plastic emergency door release comes out easily. The image shows this when clip and connector are already disconnected.

lines.text_raw: '''DO NOT FORGET TO PUT ALL THIS BACK on reassembly!'''
lines.text_rendered: DO NOT FORGET TO PUT ALL THIS BACK on reassembly!

lines.text_raw: Remove the plastic strip that protects the bottom edge.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the plastic strip that protects the bottom edge.

lines.text_raw: Unhook on the back, and tilt it forwards.
lines.text_rendered: Unhook on the back, and tilt it forwards.

lines.text_raw: Note the guiding notches to help you put it back.
lines.text_rendered: Note the guiding notches to help you put it back.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew one (T20) screw.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew one (T20) screw.

lines.text_raw: Tilt the plate back, and lift it. There is a hooked tab, and a guiding pin to help you reassemble the plate.
lines.text_rendered: Tilt the plate back, and lift it. There is a hooked tab, and a guiding pin to help you reassemble the plate.

lines.text_raw: Pull out the drain tube.
lines.text_rendered: Pull out the drain tube.

lines.text_raw: Put the cover plate aside.
lines.text_rendered: Put the cover plate aside.

lines.text_raw: Pull the power connector from the pump.
lines.text_rendered: Pull the power connector from the pump.

lines.text_raw: Using pliers, loosen the clamp on the hose from the tumbler and slide it back.
lines.text_rendered: Using pliers, loosen the clamp on the hose from the tumbler and slide it back.

lines.text_raw: Remove the hose.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the hose.

lines.text_raw: BE PREPARED FOR SOME WATER (use a towel or bowl).
lines.text_rendered: BE PREPARED FOR SOME WATER (use a towel or bowl).

lines.text_raw: In my case, the pump inlet (where we just removed the hose coming from the tumbler) was clogged with debris and some cloth.
lines.text_rendered: In my case, the pump inlet (where we just removed the hose coming from the tumbler) was clogged with debris and some cloth.

lines.text_raw: This prevented draining, and even prevented removal of the filter. Thus, requiring disassembly. But we are not done yet.
lines.text_rendered: This prevented draining, and even prevented removal of the filter. Thus, requiring disassembly. But we are not done yet.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew four T20 screws.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew four T20 screws.

lines.text_raw: Tilt the filter/pump unit (note the tab at the top), and pull it out from the back.
lines.text_rendered: Tilt the filter/pump unit (note the tab at the top), and pull it out from the back.

lines.text_raw: At his point you can clean the water inlet, the filter, and the pump. The impeller should move freely. The pump itself can also be removed to replace it (but I did not do that).
lines.text_rendered: At his point you can clean the water inlet, the filter, and the pump. The impeller should move freely. The pump itself can also be removed to replace it (but I did not do that).

lines.text_raw: In my case, a significant amount of cloth got stuck in the water inlet, including a necklace. In the filter, there were some hairpins, and inside the pump itself, a coin and a pendent. LESSON: CLEAN THE FILTER MORE OFTEN, while you can stil remove it without disassembling the machine.
